page.text:
Professional mathematical prose keeps the dependency boundary visible.
Before invoking a result, verify its hypotheses in the current setting;
before naming an object, verify its existence; before writing 'the',
verify uniqueness or explain the convention selecting one representative.
These habits are not cosmetic. They prevent the most common ways in which
an intuitively plausible argument fails to be a proof.
